title: Developer tools and the eval bench

story: Nova, our ticket-to-PR agent, finishes a backend ticket and writes "Done, all tests pass". It ran the three tests it wrote. It did not run the linter, and it did not run the older tests next to its change, one of which it broke. Nothing told it to, because "done" was only its own opinion.

The same week, a teammate adds one sentence to Nova's instructions: "before you finish, run the full test suite". Nova seems slower, and the next few pull requests look a little better. Or do they? Nobody can say, because "better" is also only an opinion.
hook.question: How do you turn "is it done?" and "did Nova get better?" into questions a machine can answer with yes or no?

p: The first answer is a command, and in a Python project commands live in pyproject.toml. poethepoet, called poe, is the Python version of npm scripts: you name a task in a [tool.poe.tasks] table and run it with uv run poe <name>, and uv run poe on its own lists every task with its help text. fcp's root pyproject.toml already has poe tasks such as cloud-up for starting the backend in Docker.

A task can be a plain command (cmd), like an npm script, or a script task that calls a Python function by its import path. A script task can also declare arguments, which become flags such as --full or --json. That matters for checks, because a check written in Python can read git, decide what to run, print a short summary and choose its exit code, which a one-line shell command does badly.

notes.text: A cmd task: a command with help text, like "test": "pytest -q" in package.json.
A script task: poe imports tools/verify.py and calls main, passing the --full flag as full.
--json makes the output one JSON object per line, for a machine to read.

read.see:
$ uv run poe
Configured tasks:
  test                  Run every test.
  verify                Lint and test what changed since main.
    --full              Lint and test everything, not only what changed.
  doctor                Check that this machine can run the project.
    --json              One JSON object per line, for machines.

read.h: verify: one answer for the editor, the agent and CI
p: verify answers "is my change done?" It finds the Python files that changed since the merge base (the commit where your branch left main), lints them, runs the tests those changes touched (with testmon from the pytest lesson), prints one line per step and exits with 1 if anything failed. --full lints and tests everything, which is what CI runs. The important part is not the script but the contract: one command, a short report and an exit code, so the answer is the same in the editor, in the agent's machine and in CI.

That exit code is how Nova learns that it is not done. Claude Code can run hooks, commands it starts at fixed moments in a session, and a Stop hook runs each time the agent wants to finish. If the hook exits with 2, Claude Code does not stop the session: it shows the agent what the hook wrote to stderr, and the agent keeps working. The hook reads its input as JSON, and when stop_hook_active is true, the agent is already continuing because of this hook, so the hook lets it stop instead of looping forever. This is guidance, not a cage: the hook does not forbid anything, it tells the agent what is still red.

notes.text: Changed .py files since the merge base, or every tracked .py file with --full.
fcp's lint rule: flake8 limited to real errors such as unused imports.
The exit code is the answer. A Stop hook and CI only need this number.

read.see:
$ uv run poe verify
Poe => verify
score.py:1:1: F401 'os' imported but unused
......                                                                   [100%]
FAIL  lint
pass  tests
$ echo '{"stop_hook_active": false}' | .claude/stop-verify.sh; echo "exit $?"
poe verify failed. Fix this before you stop:
…
exit 2

deeper.h: Go deeper: doctor, the check for the machine itself
p: A second command answers a different question: can this machine run the project at all? doctor is a list of checks, each with the fix to try: is uv installed, is Python 3.13 available, is Docker running, does .venv match uv.lock. It prints ok or FIX per check and exits with 1 if anything needs fixing. With --json it prints one JSON object per check, so a machine can read it.

That JSON form is useful far from any laptop. The image that every agent VM starts from is built every night, and running doctor --json inside the build means a broken setup fails the build instead of becoming the machine Nova works on the next morning. A fix flag can repair what is safe, such as installing a Python version, but never touches credentials or data.

read.h: The eval bench gives Nova's work a test too
p: The second question, "did Nova get better?", needs the same thing on a bigger scale: a test for the agent's whole attempt. An eval bench is a fixed set of tasks with known answers, and Harbor is a Python tool that runs an agent on each task inside a container and scores it. A Harbor task is a folder. instruction.md is what the agent reads. environment/ describes the machine it starts on, here a Dockerfile with the buggy script from the first lesson of this part. tests/test.sh runs after the agent has finished and writes a number, the reward, to /logs/verifier/reward.txt: 1 for pass, 0 for fail. The tests are copied in only for grading, so the agent never sees them.

Before a task can judge anyone, it has to prove that it can tell good work from bad. solution/solve.sh contains the known fix, and Harbor's oracle agent runs only that script, so it must score 1. Harbor's nop agent does nothing at all, so it must score 0. A task where doing nothing passes, or where the real fix fails, measures nothing and is fixed or dropped.

code.text:
pass-rate/
  instruction.md          what the agent reads: the task, in plain words
  task.toml               name, timeouts and resources
  environment/Dockerfile  the machine the agent starts on (with the bug)
  solution/solve.sh       the known fix; only the oracle agent runs it
  tests/test.sh           runs after the agent and writes the reward
  tests/check_score.py    the hidden check; copied in only for grading

notes.text: harbor init writes it. The current format starts with schema_version and a [task] table.
Only the oracle agent uses it, to prove the task can be solved.

read.see:
$ uvx harbor run -p pass-rate -a oracle
┃ Trials ┃ Exceptions ┃  Mean ┃
│      1 │          0 │ 1.000 │
$ uvx harbor run -p pass-rate -a nop
┃ Trials ┃ Exceptions ┃  Mean ┃
│      1 │          0 │ 0.000 │

p: An agent does not give the same answer every time, so each task runs several times. pass@1 is the average success rate over all those tries: the chance that one try passes. pass^3 (read "pass hat three") is the chance that three tries of the same task all pass, which measures how consistent the agent is. A task that passes once in three tries adds a third to pass@1 but nothing to pass^3.

Small benches are noisy. With 15 tasks, one task is about 6.7 points, so a drop of one task can be bad luck, and the rule is to run again; a drop of two or more is a real signal. That is how the teammate's new sentence gets a fair answer: it ships only if the score goes up on the bench. Cost and minutes per task are measured as well, but only to learn from, never as a limit on a run.

deeper.h: Go deeper: keeping the answers secret
p: A bench made from old tickets has a weakness: the real fix exists, in git history and in the merged pull request. If the agent can find it, the score measures searching, not solving. So the task checks out the commit before the fix and drops the newer history, the services the agent uses refuse to show the source pull request during a bench run, and the tasks themselves live in a restricted repository that agents and the search index can never read.

lab.title: verify, doctor and a Harbor task
lab.goal: Give the scoring project a verify and a doctor command, hook verify into a Stop hook, and write a Harbor task that scores 1 for the known fix and 0 for doing nothing.

guess.q: A Harbor task's tests/test.sh runs the hidden check, but then always writes 1 to reward.txt, whatever the check said. What do the oracle and nop agents score?

options.text: Oracle 1 and nop 0, because the hidden check still runs.
options.why: The check runs, but its result is thrown away. Only the number in reward.txt counts.

options.text: Both score 1, so the task cannot tell good work from no work.
options.why: The reward is whatever test.sh writes. That is why every task must show oracle 1 and nop 0 before it joins the bench.

options.text: Both score 0, because Harbor notices that the check failed.
options.why: Harbor does not read the check's output. It trusts the reward file.

follow.say: Write the Stop hook and feed it the JSON that Claude Code would send when the agent wants to finish.
follow.do:
mkdir -p .claude && cat > .claude/stop-verify.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Claude Code runs this when the agent wants to stop. Exit 2 sends the agent back to work.
if [ "$(jq -r '.stop_hook_active')" = "true" ]; then
  exit 0  # already continuing because of this hook: let it stop, never loop
fi
if ! output=$(uv run poe verify 2>&1); then
  echo "poe verify failed. Fix this before you stop:" >&2
  echo "$output" | tail -15 >&2
  exit 2
fi
EOF
chmod +x .claude/stop-verify.sh && echo '{"stop_hook_active": false}' | .claude/stop-verify.sh; echo "exit $?"
follow.see:
poe verify failed. Fix this before you stop:
Poe => verify
score.py:1:1: F401 'os' imported but unused
…
FAIL  lint
pass  tests
exit 2

follow.say: Now the bench. Let Harbor write a task skeleton, then fill it with the 0% bug from p10-1: the buggy script in the environment, the known fix in solve.sh and a hidden check in tests/.
follow.do:
uvx harbor init --task academy/pass-rate && cd pass-rate && rm -f tests/test_outputs.py README.md
cat > instruction.md <<'EOF'
The script /app/score.py prints the pass rate of the attempts in /app/rewards.txt.
The file holds three passes (1) and two failures (0), but the script prints 0%.
Fix score.py so that it prints the right pass rate. Do not change rewards.txt.
EOF
cat > environment/Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM python:3.13-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY score.py rewards.txt /app/
EOF
cat > environment/score.py <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path


def read_rewards(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    return path.read_text().split()


def pass_rate(rewards: list[int]) -> float:
    passed = [r for r in rewards if r == 1]
    return len(passed) / len(rewards)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    rewards = read_rewards(Path("rewards.txt"))
    print(f"pass rate: {pass_rate(rewards):.0%}")
EOF
printf '1\n0\n1\n1\n0\n' > environment/rewards.txt
cat > solution/solve.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
sed -i 's/return path.read_text().split()/return [int(r) for r in path.read_text().split()]/' /app/score.py
sed -i 's/-> list\[str\]:/-> list[int]:/' /app/score.py
EOF
cat > tests/test.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
cd /app
if python /tests/check_score.py; then
  echo 1 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
else
  echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
fi
EOF
cat > tests/check_score.py <<'EOF'
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

assert Path("/app/rewards.txt").read_text() == "1\n0\n1\n1\n0\n", "rewards.txt was changed"
out = subprocess.run(["python", "score.py"], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd="/app").stdout
assert out.strip() == "pass rate: 60%", out
print("ok:", out.strip())
EOF
chmod +x solution/solve.sh tests/test.sh && cd ..

(the task files are written)

lab.build: Write a second Harbor task, fix-tuesday, from the shared-default bug in p10-1's fix.py: failed_tasks(lines, seen: list[str] = []) still reports Monday's failure on Tuesday. Use uvx harbor init --task academy/fix-tuesday, put the buggy failed.py into environment/ with a Dockerfile, write the fix in solution/solve.sh, and a hidden check in tests/ that calls failed_tasks twice. Careful: python /tests/check_failed.py starts in /tests, so set PYTHONPATH=/app in test.sh or the import fails. Prove it: the oracle agent scores 1.000 and the nop agent 0.000.
checks: uv run poe lists test, verify (with --full) and doctor (with --json).
poe verify on the branch printed FAIL lint for the unused import and exit 1.
The Stop hook printed the failure to stderr and exited with 2; with {"stop_hook_active": true} it exits with 0.
pass-rate scores Mean 1.000 with -a oracle and 0.000 with -a nop.
fix-tuesday also scores 1.000 with oracle and 0.000 with nop.

solution.file: the fix-tuesday task, file by file
solution.text:
# fix-tuesday/instruction.md
/app/failed.py reports the tasks that failed. On Tuesday every task passed, but it still reports Monday's failure.
Fix failed_tasks so that each call only reports the failures in the lines it was given.

# fix-tuesday/environment/Dockerfile
FROM python:3.13-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY failed.py /app/

# fix-tuesday/environment/failed.py (the bug from p10-1)
def failed_tasks(lines: list[str], seen: list[str] = []) -> list[str]:
    for line in lines:
        task, reward = line.split()
        if reward == "0":
            seen.append(task)
    return seen

# fix-tuesday/solution/solve.sh
#!/bin/bash
sed -i 's/seen: list\[str\] = \[\]) -> list\[str\]:/seen: list[str] | None = None) -> list[str]:\n    seen = [] if seen is None else seen/' /app/failed.py

# fix-tuesday/tests/test.sh
#!/bin/bash
cd /app
if PYTHONPATH=/app python /tests/check_failed.py; then
  echo 1 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
else
  echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
fi

# fix-tuesday/tests/check_failed.py
from failed import failed_tasks

assert failed_tasks(["fe-bug-1 0", "be-bug-7 1"]) == ["fe-bug-1"]
assert failed_tasks(["be-bug-7 1"]) == [], "Tuesday still remembers Monday"
print("ok")

lab.fix: Someone "simplified" pass-rate/tests/test.sh to two lines: python /tests/check_score.py, then echo 1 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt. Make that change and run uvx harbor run -p pass-rate -a nop. Doing nothing now scores 1.000. Explain why the bench can no longer tell a good attempt from no attempt, and restore the if/else so the reward follows the check.
explain: Why is the exit code of poe verify more important than its printed output?
What does the Stop hook do with exit code 2, and why does it check stop_hook_active?
Why must every bench task score 1 with the oracle agent and 0 with the nop agent before it can judge Nova?
lab.done: poe verify and doctor work, the Stop hook exits 2 on a red verify, and both Harbor tasks score 1.000 for oracle and 0.000 for nop.

check.q: Nova's Stop hook runs poe verify, which fails. The hook prints the failures to stderr and exits with 2. What happens next?

options.text: The session ends, and the failures go into the pull request description.
options.why: Exit code 2 from a Stop hook blocks the stop. The session goes on.

options.text: Claude Code shows the agent the stderr text, and the agent keeps working on the failures.
options.why: That is the point of the hook: "done" becomes the command's answer, not the agent's opinion.

options.text: Claude Code retries poe verify by itself until it passes.
options.why: The hook only reports. The agent has to fix the code, and then the hook runs again at the next stop.

check.q: A new bench task scores 1.000 with the oracle agent and also 1.000 with the nop agent. What does that tell you?

options.text: The task is easy, which is fine for a smoke set.
options.why: Easy would mean a real agent passes it. Here doing nothing passes it, so it tests nothing.

options.text: The agents share a cache, so run them in a different order.
options.why: Each trial starts a fresh container. The task itself is the problem.

options.text: The hidden check does not detect the bug, so the task cannot tell good work from no work and must be fixed or dropped.
options.why: A task must fail when nothing is done (nop 0) and pass with the known fix (oracle 1).

check.q: A harness change drops the smoke bench from 11 passing tasks of 15 to 10 of 15. What is the right reaction?

options.text: Run the bench again; one task is about 6.7 points, and one task of difference can be luck.
options.why: Agents are not deterministic, and small benches are noisy. Two or more tasks lower is a real signal.

options.text: Revert the change at once, because the score went down.
options.why: One task on 15 is within the noise. Reacting to it would reject good changes by chance.

options.text: Ignore the bench; it is too small to mean anything.
options.why: It is small but useful, as long as you apply the rule: rerun on one task, act on two or more.

p: In fcp, poe verify lints the changed Python files with the project's black, isort and flake8 setup and runs the affected API tests, and npm run verify does the same for the frontend. A Stop hook in fcp's tracked .claude/settings.json runs the right one for what changed, so people's Claude Code sessions and Nova (whose harness loads the project's settings) get the same answer, and CI runs poe verify --all, the real name of the flag that this lesson's lab calls --full. poe doctor checks a developer machine, and the nightly build of the sandbox image runs it with --json so that a broken setup never reaches the agents.

The eval bench lives in ai-agents/evals, a small uv project in the TypeScript repo because Harbor is Python. TICKET-BENCH holds 40 old fcp tickets with hidden tests, each proven with nop 0 and oracle 1, and a Python adapter that runs Nova's real harness inside the task. ROUTINE-BENCH does the same for routines, for example the flaky-test fixer, the routine that finds and fixes the cause of a backend test that passes only sometimes. A 15-task smoke set runs on every harness change, scored with pass@1 and pass^3.

tickets.why: poe verify, the Stop hook in fcp's settings, and CI running the same command.
poe doctor: one line per check with its fix, a safe --fix and --json for machines.
The nightly sandbox image build runs poe doctor --json and fails on any red check.
The Harbor task format for TICKET-BENCH and the adapter that runs Nova's harness.
Curates the 40 tasks and proves each one with the nop and oracle agents.
pass@1, pass^3, cost and minutes per kind, and the smoke gate on harness changes.

words.plain: A named command in pyproject.toml's [tool.poe.tasks], run with uv run poe <name>; Python's npm scripts.
A command Claude Code runs when the agent wants to finish; exit code 2 sends the agent back to work.
A folder with an instruction, an environment, a known solution and tests that write a reward.
The number a task's tests/test.sh writes to /logs/verifier/reward.txt: 1 for pass, 0 for fail.
Harbor's two proof agents: oracle runs the known fix (must score 1), nop does nothing (must score 0).
The chance one try passes, and the chance three tries of the same task all pass.

review.q: Write the poe line for a script task verify that calls tools.verify:main with a boolean --full flag.
review.a: verify = { script = "tools.verify:main(full=full)", args = [{ name = "full", type = "boolean" }], help = "..." } under [tool.poe.tasks].

review.q: List the files of a Harbor task and say who reads each one.
review.a: instruction.md (the agent), task.toml (Harbor), environment/ (Harbor builds the agent's machine), solution/solve.sh (only the oracle agent), tests/test.sh and the hidden checks (the verifier, after the agent).

review.q: A task passes in 1 of 3 tries. What does it add to pass@1 and to pass^3?
review.a: A third (0.33) to the task's pass@1, and 0 to its pass^3, because the three tries did not all pass.

remember: Make "done" and "better" into commands with a yes or no answer: verify's exit code for a change, and a reward that is 1 for the known fix and 0 for doing nothing for an agent.
